post.description:
Suggest resources to add to a blueprint based on a natural-language prompt.

Walks anchor resource types in priority order (journey > workflow_definition >
automation_flow > schema > entity-backed types) and returns matches per
anchor using each upstream API's text search. Suggestions are marked
`is_root: true` so callers can pass `add_dependencies=true` to
bulkAddBlueprintResources and have transitive dependencies resolved
server-side — which means a single matched journey can stand in for its
full product/schema/template bundle.

No side effects on the blueprint — the caller persists the chosen resources
via the existing create/bulk-add endpoints.

get.description: List all blueprint jobs

Poll the current state of a job. Serves both Terraform (v2) and V3-engine jobs —
check `sync_engine` (`terraform` | `v3`) to tell them apart. V3 jobs additionally
expose live `resource_progress[]`. V3 single-install and bulk-install child jobs
are polled here.

post.description:
Resume an installation job that is paused at `status: "WAITING_USER_ACTION"` after
planning. Works for both Terraform and V3 jobs. Not needed for V3 installs created
with `auto_apply: true` (including all bulk-install child jobs), which apply
without pausing.

This call applies the plan. Callers acting for a user — AI agents in particular —
must show the user the job's `resource_progress[]` (`impact_on_install` and
`impact_on_install_reason`) and call it only once the user has approved.

Also resumes a V3 install paused at `status: "REAUTH_REQUIRED"`, where the
caller's credentials could not safely cover another run. The job keeps its
`job_id`, so resuming continues from the operation-log checkpoint rather than
re-applying completed work. The request's bearer token becomes the destination
credential; for a cross-org install whose SOURCE credential also expired, send a
freshly scoped source token as `source_auth_token` — the destination bearer is not
a valid substitute for it.

Retry a finished V3 installation job whose status is `FAILED` or
`PARTIAL_SUCCESS`. Starts a fresh install job (new `job_id`) with the same
source/destination and `auto_apply: true` — no `:continue` call is needed.
For an AI-agent caller the new job instead pauses at the plan
(`WAITING_USER_ACTION`) for the user to approve via `:continue`.
The plan phase re-resolves every resource: already-synced resources no-op,
so effectively only the failed resources are re-applied.

Must be called by a user of the destination org (where the job lives); the
caller's bearer token is used as the destination token. The plan reuses the
manifest persisted by the original install, so no source-org access is
required. The original job's `options` (ignored resources, sync_notes) are
reused when present; older jobs without persisted options fall back to the
destination blueprint's `ignored_resource_addresses`.

post.description: Lists what the update wrote, from its own journal, and what reverting each resource would do. Resources changed since the update need an explicit choice (`requires_choice`); `not_restorable` ones can only be kept. The preview is immutable: a new call returns a new `revert_preview_id`. Only an `applied` or `partially_applied` plan inside its revert window has a preview, and only while no later update owns any of its resources.

post.description: Reverts the update as the preview describes it, with an explicit `action` for every preview entry. Starts a `restore` job and moves the plan to `reverting`; the job ends it `reverted`, or `revert_partial` when a resource changed meanwhile or failed. Replaying the same `idempotency_key` returns the same job.

post.description:
Install a blueprint into a single destination org using the V3 engine (direct API
calls, no Terraform). Creates resources in topological order with global ID
replacement and supports checkpoint-based resume on failure.

**Lifecycle (how to drive an install to completion):**
1. `POST /v3/blueprint-manifest/blueprint:install` returns `{ job_id }` (202).
2. Poll the job with `GET /v2/blueprint-manifest/jobs/{job_id}` — V3 jobs are
   served by the same v2 jobs endpoints as Terraform jobs and are identified by
   `sync_engine: "v3"`. Watch `status` and `resource_progress[]`.
3. If `auto_apply` is `false` (default), the job pauses at
   `status: "WAITING_USER_ACTION"` after planning. Review the plan before resuming:
   each `resource_progress[]` entry carries `impact_on_install` (`create`, `update`,
   `no-op`, `error`) and, where relevant, `impact_on_install_reason`. Resume it with
   `POST /v2/blueprint-manifest/jobs/{job_id}:continue` once the plan is approved.
4. If `auto_apply` is `true`, the engine applies automatically after plan +
   snapshot — no `:continue` call is needed. This is what the bulk-install worker
   uses; to install into many orgs at once prefer `POST .../bulk-installs`.

**AI agents** (tokens such as "Connect ChatGPT to epilot") cannot use
`auto_apply` (403). Install without it, show the user the plan, and call
`:continue` only after the user approves it.

**The plan fails instead of pausing** (`status: "FAILED"`, error code
`missing_required_reference`) when a resource references something that is
neither in the blueprint nor in the destination org and the destination API
would reject it — for example a workflow whose automation tasks point at
automations the package does not contain. Fix it in the source blueprint: add
the missing resources (refreshing the blueprint picks up dependencies) and
publish again. Keep resources in the blueprint even when they already exist in
the destination; an existing resource is matched and updated, not duplicated,
and removing it leaves everything that references it pointing at an id the
destination does not have. Alternatively pass the blocked addresses in
`options.resources_to_ignore` to install the rest.

For cross-org installs, pass `destination_auth_token` (the destination org's
token); reads use the caller's bearer token, writes use that token.

source_blueprint_file.description: S3 key to the blueprint zip file

destination_auth_token.description: Auth token for the destination org. Required for cross-org installs where the caller's token belongs to the source org. Defaults to the caller's bearer token.

auto_apply.description:
When `true`, the install skips the manual plan-approval step and applies
straight after plan + snapshot succeed (no `:continue` call needed).
Defaults to `false`. Used internally by the bulk-install worker.
Rejected with 403 for AI-agent callers, whose installs must be approved
by the user at the plan step.

session_credentials.description:
Lets the install refresh the caller's session on its own, so a run that
outlives the ~60 minute token lifetime continues without the user present.
Held server-side for the job's lifetime, referenced from the state machine
rather than embedded in it, and deleted when the job finishes.

Optional. Without it an install that outruns its token pauses at
`status: "REAUTH_REQUIRED"` and waits to be resumed through
`POST /v2/blueprint-manifest/jobs/{job_id}:continue`.

Bounded by the refresh token itself (18 hours), not unlimited.

refresh_token.description: Cognito refresh token for the caller, scoped to the source org.

client_id.description:
The Cognito app client the refresh token was issued for. Required because
epilot provisions one user pool and app client per organization at
runtime, so the service cannot derive it.

pipeline_id.description:
Cross-org installs only. The destination credential is not a Cognito
session — it is minted from the refreshed source session through
sandbox-api, so it is re-derived per continuation instead of stored.

Location.description: Path to poll the resulting job: GET /v2/blueprint-manifest/jobs/{job_id}

400.description: Missing required source or destination fields

post.description:
Roll a deployment back to its pre-install state. Two phases:

  1. Upsert — re-applies the captured payloads via snapshot-api's
     `:restore` (server-side; runs config-engine.apply with captured
     target ids pre-seeded). Skipped for pure-create deployments
     whose snapshot was empty.
  2. Delete sweep — for lineage rows of this blueprint instance not
     present in the snapshot's captured set, deletes the live
     resource via the type's adapter. Co-ownership / drift /
     no-delete-capability skip the entry with the corresponding
     reason.

Resolves `(blueprint_id, job_id)` to the entry in
`Blueprint.deployments[]` and reads its `snapshot_id` and
`destination_blueprint_id` — the caller never needs to handle
snapshot ids directly.

Async — returns 202 with a job id. Poll the job to track progress.
The restore holds its own per-instance lock (`active_restore_job_id`),
separate from `installation_status`. Starting a restore is rejected with
409 when another restore already holds that lock, or when an install is
running (`installation_status === 'IN_PROGRESS'`). Keeping the two locks
distinct keeps installs and reverts decoupled: an in-flight or failed
restore never overwrites `installation_status`, which keeps reflecting
the actual install outcome (and drives the install badge in the
Blueprints overview) throughout the revert.

400.description: Deployment has no snapshot, or the snapshot is not in a `completed` state.

404.description: Blueprint not found, or no deployment with the given job_id on this blueprint.

409.description:
Another install or restore is in flight for this blueprint instance. For a merge
deployment also: `merge_snapshot_restore_unavailable` (its plan is not `failed` /
`partially_applied`, or the snapshot or revert window is gone),
`revert_newer_update_first`, `merge_plan_state_conflict` (a merge revert holds the plan) or
`blueprint_update_in_progress` (another writer holds the Blueprint).

get.description:
Computes what would happen if the user triggered a restore on this
deployment, without performing any writes. The forecast uses the
snapshot's captured resources (when present) plus the current lineage
state plus per-adapter gates (co-ownership, no-delete-capability,
heuristic-match, drift when wired).

Idempotent and side-effect free. Safe to call repeatedly. The result
may shift between calls if operators edit destination resources or
another blueprint adopts a shared resource in the meantime.

post.description:
Starts a read-only health scan of the resources this deployment's
blueprint instance tracks in the destination org (see
docs/rfcs/RFC-org-health-check.md, Phase 0). Checks:

  - live readability — every lineage-tracked resource is read back
    via its adapter; tracked-but-unreadable resources are flagged.
  - referential integrity — destination payloads containing
    unreplaced source-org ids, or references to tracked resources
    that are not readable.
  - install completeness — install operations whose final attempt
    ended `failed` or `skipped`, with their rejection reasons.

Async — returns 202 immediately with a `running` report stub. Poll
the health-report endpoint until `status` is `completed` or
`failed`. Never mutates any resource.

post.description:
Install one source blueprint into many destination organizations in a single
request. The server schedules child V3 installs with `auto_apply=true` and caps
active installs at `max_concurrency`. Not available to AI-agent callers (403),
since no child install pauses for the user to approve its plan. Per-target failures are isolated and
retryable; they do not stop the remaining targets.

Each target carries its own write-only `destination_auth_token` (org-scoped).
Tokens are passed to the worker via Step Functions input only — they are never
persisted in DynamoDB nor returned by any endpoint.

get.description:
List all custom uniqueness criteria configured for the caller's organization.
These overrides are applied during install (V2 and V3) when matching incoming
resources against existing ones in the destination org, replacing the default
per-resource-type field set with the caller's chosen fields (AND-combined).

defaults.description:
Built-in default uniqueness fields per resource type, as used by
the install engines when no custom criteria are configured.

readonly_types.description:
Resource types whose criteria are fixed by epilot and cannot be
customized (writes are rejected). Shown read-only in the UI.

Set or replace the uniqueness criteria for a resource type. The provided fields
must be valid attributes on the resource's schema (the UI typically loads the
schema to populate options). All listed fields are AND-combined during matching.

propagated_to.description:
Org IDs this rule was also applied to (the UI's "Also apply to"
selection). Stored so the selection survives reloads; each target
org still holds its own criteria row.

BlueprintNote.description: A single internal note on a blueprint.

text.example: Adjusted the meter-reading journey for the §14a rollout.

updated_at.description: Set the first time the note text is edited.

preinstall.description: Markdown content shown before starting to install the blueprint

notes.description:
Internal collaboration notes, oldest first. Each entry is stamped with
its author and creation time server-side; an edit rewrites only `text`
and stamps `updated_at`, so the history of who noted what stays intact.
Written via `addBlueprintNote` / `updateBlueprintNote` /
`deleteBlueprintNote`, not by `updateBlueprint`.

Available on every blueprint including marketplace ones (whose
`description` is read-only), and never included in the published
marketplace package — see `buildMetadata` in
`services/blueprint-v3/published-blueprint.ts`. Carried to a
destination org only when an install/sync passes
`options.sync_notes: true`.

job_id.description: Blueprint installation job that created or updated this deployment record

performed_by.description:
Who actually ran this synchronization — the caller of the install job.
Absent on deployments recorded before this field existed; consumers
should fall back to the blueprint's `updated_by` for those.

merge_snapshot_id.description:
The fail-closed pre-apply snapshot of a merge deployment. Set instead of `snapshot_id`;
the whole-deployment restore of a merge deployment restores it.

snapshot_restore_available.description:
Merge deployments only (absent otherwise). True when the whole-deployment restore
(`POST /v3/blueprint-manifest/blueprints/{blueprint_id}/deployments/{job_id}:restore`) may run for it: its plan ended `failed` or
`partially_applied`, the merge snapshot exists, the revert window is open and no
restore ran or runs for it. That restore applies every resource the snapshot captured
(edits made after the update are overwritten), invalidates the update's merge evidence
(the next update plans those resources two-way) and leaves the plan `reverted` or
`revert_partial`, after which "Revert this update" is no longer offered. The endpoint
answers 409 `merge_snapshot_restore_unavailable` otherwise, and
`revert_newer_update_first` when a later deployment changed the destination.

revert_until.description: Last moment the merge update of this deployment can be reverted.

restore_details.description: Restore lifecycle metadata for this deployment.

has_revertible_changes.description:
Whether this sync changed destination resources in a way that can
be reverted. `false` means the sync completed without create,
update, internal-update, or delete impacts, so there is no revert
action to offer.

resource_impact_summary.description: Counts of resource impact values from the V3 apply result.

last_restore_job_id.description:
BlueprintInstallationJob id of the most recent restore that ran
against this deployment. Used by the FE to keep the restore-status
badge visible across page reloads. Frontends poll this job to
render the latest restore outcome.

last_restore_at.description:
Timestamp of the most recent restore that ran against this
deployment. Stamped when the restore sweep finishes. Used by the
FE to show when a sync was reverted.

last_restored_by.description:
Identity of the caller who triggered the most recent restore.
Stamped when the restore sweep finishes. Used by the FE to show
who reverted a sync.

name.description: Display name (email or token name) of the restorer.

user_id.description: User id of the restorer, when triggered by a user.

is_verified.description: Whether the blueprint is verified by epilot

ignored_resource_addresses.description: Resource addresses excluded during the latest install/update and ignored by verification.

active_restore_job_id.description:
ID of the restore (revert) job currently holding a lock on this
blueprint instance's resources, or null/absent when no revert is
running. Deliberately separate from `installation_status`: installs
and reverts stay decoupled, so a revert must not overwrite install
health — `installation_status` keeps reflecting the actual install
outcome (and drives the install badge in the Blueprints overview)
for the duration of the revert.

active_restore_started_at.description:
ISO timestamp of when the current restore lock
(`active_restore_job_id`) was acquired, or null/absent when no revert
is running. Written and cleared alongside `active_restore_job_id`.
Lets the lock self-expire: a lock older than the staleness threshold
(whose job never completed the sweep, e.g. the state machine was
aborted) is treated as stale so a new revert can proceed instead of
being blocked forever.

source_blueprint_id.description: ID of the blueprint that brought this blueprint to the destination org (deployed or installed)

archived.description: Whether the blueprint is archived (soft-deleted). Archived blueprints are hidden from the main list.

recommended_apps.description: List of recommended app IDs for the blueprint

enabled.description: Features that must be enabled in the target org

disabled.description: Features that must be disabled in the target org

zip_file_name.description: Custom name for the exported zip file

prompt.description: Natural-language description of what to include.
prompt.example: everything for the hausanschluss use case

blueprint_id.description:
When provided, suggestions are scoped as additions to this existing
blueprint — resources already in it are excluded from the response.

resources.description: Suggested resources to add. All marked is_root so the caller can request transitive dependency resolution.

suggested_blueprint_name.description:
Short title derived from the prompt. Useful when the caller is
creating a new blueprint as a result of the suggestion — saves the
user from naming it themselves.

explanation.description: Short human-readable summary of what was matched and why.

add_dependencies_recommended.description:
Hint to the caller: persist via bulkAddBlueprintResources with
?add_dependencies=true so anchor resources (journeys, workflows)
pull their transitive dependencies.

SkippedBlueprintResource.description:
A resource that was requested (or discovered as a dependency) but was not
added to the Blueprint. Reasons are stable machine-readable codes.

is_root.description: When a resource is marked as root, we'll be able to keep track of it's dependencies

is_ready.description: when editing a blueprint, this indicates if the resource is ready to be exported and when installing a blueprint, this indicates if the resource is ready to be used

is_hidden.description: When a resource is marked as hidden, it's used to hide it from the UI

is_disabled.description: When a resource is marked as disabled, it will be skipped during export

parent_resource_ids.description: Used to automatically remove resources with hard dependencies and to block deletion of resources with hard dependencies

depends_on_addresses.description: Terraform addresses this resource references (for dependency-aware ignore)

impact_on_install_reason.description: Fields causing the updates / internal updates on a resource install

impact_on_install_changes.description:
Both sides' values per `impact_on_install_reason` entry. Present only
when the install was started with `options.include_field_diffs`.

destination.description:
The destination organization's current value. Absent when the
destination has no value there. A value above 4KB is replaced
by the string `__epilot_value_too_large__`.

source.description: The value the sync would write. Absent when the source drops the field.

added.description: True when the destination has no value at this path.

impact_on_install_labels.description:
Human-readable label per `impact_on_install_reason` entry, keyed by that
entry, from the resource type's adapter (config-engine `diff.describe`).
Only entries whose label differs from the raw path; absent when the
adapter provides none.

impact_on_install_summary.description:
One or two lines summarizing the change set, from the resource type's
adapter (config-engine `diff.summarize`). Absent when the adapter provides none.

BlueprintPreview.description: Preview data for a blueprint before installation. Stored temporarily with TTL.

sync_engine.description: Engine that must install this preview, detected from the uploaded archive's own format (never from a feature flag or request parameter). `v3` is only reported for a correctly shaped and validly signed V3 package. Clients must install a `v3` preview through `POST /v3/blueprint-manifest/blueprint:install` and a `terraform` preview through `POST /v2/blueprint-manifest/blueprints:install`. Absent only on previews created before format detection shipped; treat an absent value as `terraform`.

blueprint_file_s3_key.description: S3 key of the blueprint zip file

is_updating.description: Whether the blueprint is updating to the latest version in the marketplace

recommended_apps.description: List of recommended app IDs for the blueprint

has_update_available.description: Whether a newer version is available in the marketplace.

latest_marketplace_version.description: The latest version available in the marketplace.

installation_link.description: URL to install/update the blueprint from the marketplace.

InstalledMarketplaceBlueprintItem.description: Summary of an installed marketplace blueprint for version tracking

slug.description: URL slug of the blueprint from the epilot marketplace

has_update_available.description: Whether a newer version is available in the marketplace

latest_marketplace_version.description: The latest version available in the marketplace

installation_link.description: URL to install/update the blueprint from the marketplace

sync_engine.description: Engine used for this install job

resource_progress.description: Per-resource live status. Populated only for V3 installs.

merge_plan_id.description: The update merge plan of this job, when it updates journeys by merging.

wait_kind.description: What a WAITING_USER_ACTION or REAUTH_REQUIRED job waits for.

prefill_from_merge_plan_id.description: The earlier merge plan whose choices prefill this job's plan (Refresh or retry).

assigned_merge_plan_id.description: The id Refresh reserved for this job's merge plan.

BulkInstallStatus.description:
Aggregate status for a bulk install or one of its targets.
- `QUEUED`: not started yet
- `IN_PROGRESS`: at least one target queued/in-progress, not all done
- `SUCCESS`: all targets succeeded
- `PARTIAL_SUCCESS`: all targets terminal with a mix of success/partial/failure
- `FAILED`: all targets terminal and none succeeded or partially succeeded
- `REVIEW_REQUIRED` (targets only): the update merges journeys and waits for review in the
  update wizard (`merge_plan_id`). Terminal for the bulk install, which never applies it.

BulkInstallCounts.description: Tally of target rows by status. Recomputed from target rows on each transition.

BulkInstall.description: Bulk install parent. Never carries target auth tokens.

BulkInstallTarget.description:
A single destination of a bulk install. `job` is the hydrated latest child
install job derived from `job_ids.at(-1)`. Auth tokens are never stored or returned.

merge_plan_id.description: The merge plan to review when `status` is `REVIEW_REQUIRED`.

job.description: The hydrated latest child install job (`job_ids.at(-1)`), when present.

next_cursor.description: Opaque cursor for the next page. Absent on the last page.

destination_auth_token.description: Write-only org-scoped token for the destination org. Never persisted or returned.

source_org_id.description:
The org that owns the source blueprint. Optional; defaults to the caller org and,
if provided, must equal it — source reads use the caller's token, and the bulk job
is owned/polled by the caller org. A different value is rejected with 400.

max_concurrency.description: Maximum number of concurrently active child installs.

install_job_id.description:
The install job whose deployment is being reverted. Maps back
to the entry in `Blueprint.deployments[]`.

merge_plan_id.description: Set on the revert of a merge update; the plan's state follows the revert.

snapshot_id.description:
The snapshot driving Phase 1 of the restore. Null for sweep-only
restores (pure-create deployments with no captured manifest).

restore_result.description: Absent while the job is still IN_PROGRESS.

error_code.description:
Stable machine code for a failed resource, when config-engine threw a
typed error. Keys a translation in the Blueprints UI; `error_message`
is the English fallback when absent or unrecognised.

error_data.description: Interpolation values for the translated `error_code` message.

action.description:
On `restore-preview`: the action the restore would take.
On `restore_result`: the action that was applied.
`failed` only appears on `restore_result`.

reason.description:
Only set when `action == skip`. `not_created_by_install` means the
resource was neither captured for overwrite nor created by this install,
so the revert leaves the pre-existing resource unchanged.
`non_revertible` means the snapshot holds no restorable copy, so the revert
neither restores nor deletes the resource: a secret type (`access_token`,
`environment_variable`), which is never captured; a `file` or
`document_template` that existed before the install but that the snapshot
skipped (e.g. `content_identity_missing`, or content archiving not enabled
for the org); or a `file` or `document_template` this install created while
the org's new content adapter flag is off.
`unconfirmed` means the snapshot restore was partial and no per-resource
outcome is available. It does not assert that the resource was left unchanged.
`unknown_provenance` means the install result is unavailable, so creation
by this specific install cannot be proved and the resource is not deleted.

last_synced_at.description: Only set when `reason == modified`. From the lineage row's last install write.

current_updated_at.description: Only set when `reason == modified`. From the destination resource's current state.

is_hidden.description:
Mirrors the install manifest's `is_hidden` for this resource —
helper resources (entity mappings, datasources, flow-template
automations) the UI hides on every other resources view. Absent
on rows from legacy installs without a persisted manifest.

co_owned_by.description:
Only set when `reason == co_owned`. The other live blueprint
instances that still own this resource's lineage row — the
"another sync" the skip refers to.

protected_by.description:
Only set when `reason == dependency_protected`. The surviving
resource(s) whose 'hard' reference to this one is why it wasn't
deleted (e.g. a skipped Journey still triggering this Automation).

resource_name.description: Human-readable name of the affected resource

verdict.description: Mechanical root-cause classification and suggested fix, when determinable

evidence.description: Check-specific evidence, e.g. the JSON path and referenced id of a broken reference.

referenced_name.description: Human-readable name or logical slug of the referenced source resource

referenced_lineage_id.description: Logical source lineage identity of the referenced resource

expected_target_id.description: Destination id that should have replaced the source reference

reference_kind.description: Human-readable description of the exact field carrying the reference

known_blind_spots.description: Type-specific contracts the current scanner explicitly does not claim to validate.

html_url.description: Presigned link to the rendered HTML report (present once the check completed)

snapshot_id.description:
The snapshot driving Phase 1 of the restore. Null/absent for
sweep-only restores (pure-create deployments with no captured
manifest).

has_effective_changes.description:
`true` iff at least one entry in `resources` has an effective
action (`action` is `restore` or `delete`). `false` when every
resource would be skipped (all `skip` / `failed`). Consumers
can gate the "Revert sync" confirm button on this — if false,
executing the revert is a no-op.

job_id.description: The install job whose deployment is being previewed.

error.description: Why the preview failed. Present only when `status` is `failed`.

installation_job_id.description: Install job this verification is checking, when known.

sync_engine.description: Install engine used by the linked installation job, when known.

resource_results_s3_key.description: S3 key for detailed results when too large for inline storage.

failure_context.description: Explains whether this result is likely downstream of another failed resource.

path.description: JSON path to the differing field (e.g. "steps[2].name")

resources_to_ignore.description: List of resource addresses to ignore changes for. When a resource is marked as create, it will be ignored and not created.

sync_notes.description:
When `true`, the source blueprint's `notes` overwrite the destination
blueprint's `notes`. Defaults to `false`, which leaves the
destination's notes untouched.

include_field_diffs.description:
When `true`, the plan records both sides' values for every changed
field of an `update` resource (`impact_on_install_changes`). Read at
plan time, so it must be set on `:install`. Defaults to `false`; the
values make the plan considerably larger.

source_auth_token.description:
A freshly issued bearer for the SOURCE organization, used only when resuming a
job paused at `REAUTH_REQUIRED` whose source credential also expired. Applies to
cross-org installs: apply-time reads such as the authenticated File API fallback
for private source files run against the source org, so the destination bearer
cannot stand in for them. Omit it to keep the source token the job already has.

MergePlanState.description: Lifecycle state of an update merge plan.

MergeChoice.description: The reviewer's choice for one decision group. Valid only while `group_signature` matches.

MergeChoiceInput.description: A submitted choice. `option_id` is not an enum here, so an option the group does not offer is answered with 422 `merge_plan_choice_invalid` and its `group_ids`, like every other invalid choice.

MergeSectionValue.description: A unit value in builder terms. `present` false means the unit does not exist on that side.

kind.description: `confirm` is a whole-resource group with a single valid option the reviewer confirms.

MergePlanReview.description: Summary of an update merge plan.

plan_revision.description: Send back as `expected_plan_revision` when saving choices or applying.

expected_plan_revision.description: Equal to `plan_revision`; the value the next write sends back.

warnings.description: Non-blocking findings of every journey of the plan.

blocked_reasons.description: Reasons that block the whole plan. Blocked journeys carry their own `blocking_reasons`.

apply_counts_unknown.description: True when the apply ended without a readable journal. `apply_counts` are then zeros, not real counts.

other_resource_count.description: Resources other than journeys, updated as in an ordinary install.

revert_until.description: Last moment the applied update can be reverted.

successor_failed.description: Refresh produced no plan and this plan could not be restored (its review wait had ended). Refresh the Blueprint to plan the update again.

MergePlanApplyCounts.description: Journeys by what apply does with the current choices: `updated` (written), `kept` (blocked, left as they are), `removed` (stay removed), `restored` (created again).

MergeResourceOutcome.description: Result of one journey after apply.

MergePlanRevisionRequest.description: Body of discard and refresh requests.

merge_plan_id.description: Id the successor plan is stored under once its job has planned.

category.description: Display grouping. `unchanged`: as the update left it. `changed_since_update`: edited since (restoring overwrites that edit). `created_by_update`: created by the update (restore removes it). `metadata_only`: a journey the update kept removed (restore resets only its update history). `not_restorable`: keep-only (no captured content, deleted since, or an unsupported type).

requires_choice.description: The revert must name this entry's action explicitly.

selections.description: One action for every entry of the preview.

session_credentials.description: Lets the revert refresh the caller's session on its own, as on install. Held server-side for the job's lifetime and deleted when it finishes.

group_ids.description: The decision groups the error is about.

action.description: The plan can no longer be applied as it is; Refresh plans the update again.

merge_plan_id.description: The merge plan to review, when a job endpoint refuses a job that waits for one.

retry_after.description: Seconds after which a `blueprint_update_in_progress` conflict is worth retrying.

resource_keys.description: The revert preview entries the error is about.
